label: hemorrhagic anovulatory follicle
reason: Describes a pathological/dysfunctional state (hemorrhagic + anovulatory = failed to ovulate with bleeding). UBERON covers normal anatomy only; pathological structures belong in MONDO or as PATO-qualified terms.
suggestion: Consider MONDO or create a PATO-qualified term for this abnormal follicle state. The existing DOI references (10.1093/oxfordjournals.humrep.a136365, 10.1210/er.2018-00085) may be useful for documenting the pathological condition in the appropriate ontology.

label: luteinized unruptured follicle
reason: Describes a pathological/dysfunctional state (luteinized but unruptured = failed to rupture and release oocyte despite luteinization). UBERON covers normal anatomy only; this represents ovulatory dysfunction.
suggestion: Consider MONDO or create a PATO-qualified term for this abnormal follicle state. This condition is also known as luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome (LUFS). The existing DOI references (10.1093/oxfordjournals.humrep.a136365, 10.1210/er.2018-00085) document this pathological condition.

label: matrisome
reason: The matrisome is a molecular/proteomic concept referring to the complete set of extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins and ECM-associated proteins in a tissue or organism, not an anatomical structure. UBERON is an anatomy ontology focused on structural entities.
suggestion: This term belongs in a protein ontology (PRO - Protein Ontology) or a molecular function/component ontology (GO - Gene Ontology). The term was coined in 2009-2010 by the Hynes laboratory to describe the ECM proteome. While ECM is an important component of many anatomical structures in UBERON, the matrisome as a conceptual collection of proteins is outside UBERON's scope.
